trial_court: Court of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Bathinda
case_name: Lakhwinder Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Lakhwinder Singh and others (husband, wife, etc.)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner No.1 Lakhwinder Singh's marriage to respondent No.2 Chinderpal Kaur was dissolved by mutual consent under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Respondent No.2 filed an application under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which was pending in the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: When the relationship of husband and wife ceases to exist after obtaining a decree of divorce, the application filed under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act does not survive.
legal_principles.held: On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 has argued that the decree of divorce was obtained by petitioner No.1 by playing fraud upon respondent No.2. The petitioners have committed domestic violence upon the complainant, therefore, they have rightly been summoned to face trial by the Court.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 12

legal_principles.principle: A decree of divorce obtained by mutual consent under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, is conclusive evidence that the marriage has irretrievably broken down.
legal_principles.held: It was specifically pleaded by them that they have been living separately from each other for the last about two years. Their marriage has irretrievably broken down and there is no chance of their living together in future.

outcome.final_order: The complaint and summoning order were quashed.

keywords: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
